method_card.title: Probability Basics & Tree Diagrams
method_card.content:
Probability ranges from 0 (impossible) to 1 (certain). \(P(A) = \frac{\text{favourable outcomes}}{\text{total outcomes}}\). \(P(\text{not } A) = 1 - P(A)\).

Expected frequency = probability × number of trials. Relative frequency = observed frequency ÷ trials (gets closer to theoretical with more trials).

Tree diagrams: Multiply along branches (AND), add between branches (OR). For independent events, probabilities don't change. For without replacement, adjust the denominator.
method_card.example:
A bag has 3 red and 5 blue balls. Find P(red).

\(P(\text{red}) = \frac{3}{3+5} = \frac{3}{8}\)

steps: Split the event into every path that works, e.g. red-blue AND blue-red.
Multiply along each path, then add the paths.
'At least one' is quickest as \(1 - P(\text{none})\).

gold.hint: Two orders give one of each: red then blue, and blue then red. Add them.
gold.display: A bag has 7 red and 5 blue. Two are picked without replacement. Find P(one of each colour) as a fraction.

guided_steps.say: One of each can happen two ways: red then blue, or blue then red. Without replacement.

guided_steps.hint: Reds times blues along the path.

guided_steps.say: P(blue-red) works out the same, 35/132. Two paths, so add them.
Add the tops.

misconceptions.message: One of each happens two ways: red-blue AND blue-red, each 35/132. Add them: 70/132 = 35/66. One order alone is 35/132.

gold.hint: Three reds without replacement: reds and total both drop each pick.
gold.display: A bag has 8 red and 4 blue. Three are picked without replacement. Find P(all red) as a fraction.

guided_steps.say: Three reds without replacement: reds and total drop each pick.

guided_steps.hint: One red and one ball removed.

guided_steps.say: Multiply bottoms, then simplify 336/1320 (divide by 24).

misconceptions.message: The reds drop each pick: 8/12 × 7/11 × 6/10 = 14/55. Treating it as 8/12 cubed gives 8/27.

gold.hint: Add the two routes to B: through A and through not A.
gold.display: P(A) = 0.6, P(B given A) = 0.5, P(B given not A) = 0.2. Find P(B) as a fraction.

guided_steps.say: B can be reached two ways: through A, or through not A. Total-probability rule.

guided_steps.hint: P(not A) times P(B given not A).

guided_steps.say: Add the paths: 0.30 + 0.08 = 0.38 = 38/100. Simplify by 2.

misconceptions.message: B can arrive two ways. Add them: 0.5×0.6 + 0.2×0.4 = 0.38 = 19/50. The A path alone is 0.30 = 3/10.

gold.hint: Easier as 1 minus P(no heads at all).
gold.display: A coin is flipped 4 times. Find P(at least one head) as a fraction.

guided_steps.say: At least one head is easiest as 1 − P(no heads at all).
So P(no heads) = 1/16, and P(at least one) = 16/16 − 1/16.
Subtract the tops.

misconceptions.message: At least one head = 1 − P(no heads) = 1 − 1/16 = 15/16. 1/16 is the chance of NO heads.

gold.hint: Exactly one head means head-then-tail or tail-then-head; add both.
gold.display: A biased coin has P(H) = ⅔. It is flipped twice. Find P(exactly one head) as a fraction.

guided_steps.say: Biased coin: P(H) = 2/3, so P(T) = 1/3. Exactly one head is HT or TH.
P(TH) is the same, 2/9. Two paths, so add.
Add the tops.

misconceptions.message: Exactly one head is HT OR TH: 2/9 + 2/9 = 4/9. One order alone is 2/9.

bronze.hint: Count the reds, then divide by the total number of balls.
bronze.display: A bag has 5 red and 3 blue balls. Find P(red) as a fraction.

guided_steps.say: Probability is favourable outcomes over the total. Start by counting.
So P(red) = favourable over total. Now write the fraction.
guided_steps.hint: The number of reds you counted.

guided_steps.pre: Check: 5 out of 8, and 5/8 is already simplest. Type the numerator once more:

misconceptions.message: Probability is favourable over the TOTAL, not over the rest. There are 5 red out of 8 balls, so P(red) = 5/8. Writing 5/3 compares reds to blues instead.

bronze.hint: Even numbers on a dice are 2, 4 and 6, out of six faces.
bronze.display: A fair dice is rolled. Find P(even number).

guided_steps.say: A fair dice has faces 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6. Count the even ones.
So P(even) = 3/6. That simplifies: divide top and bottom by 3.

bronze.hint: P(not win) = 1 minus P(win); turn the decimal into a fraction.
bronze.display: A spinner has P(win) = 0.4. Find P(not win) as a fraction.

guided_steps.say: P(not win) means everything except winning: 1 − P(win).

guided_steps.hint: One take away nought point four.

guided_steps.say: Now turn 0.6 into a fraction. 0.6 = 6/10, then simplify by 2.

misconceptions.message: That is P(win). The question asks P(not win) = 1 − 0.4 = 0.6 = 3/5.

bronze.hint: Favourable over total: toffees over all the sweets.
bronze.display: There are 12 sweets: 7 toffee and 5 mint. Find P(toffee) as a fraction.

guided_steps.say: Favourable over total. The toffees are what we want.
So P(toffee) = toffees over total.

misconceptions.message: Put toffees over the TOTAL of 12 sweets: 7/12. 7/5 compares toffees to mints instead.

bronze.hint: Count the red sections over the total number of sections.
bronze.display: A spinner has 5 equal sections. 2 of them are red. Find P(red) as a fraction.

guided_steps.say: Favourable over total. Each equal section is one outcome.
So P(red) = reds over total.

misconceptions.message: Put red sections over the TOTAL of 5: 2/5. 2/3 compares red to non-red instead.

bronze.hint: Add up all the balls for the total, then put greens over it.
bronze.display: A bag has 2 red, 3 green and 5 blue. Find P(green).

guided_steps.say: Total everything first, then put greens over the total.
So P(green) = greens over total.

misconceptions.message: Total the balls first: 2 + 3 + 5 = 10, so P(green) = 3/10. 3/7 compares green to the others.

bronze.hint: Expected number = probability × number of trials.
bronze.display: P(rain) = 0.2. The event is repeated 50 times. Find the expected number of rainy days.

guided_steps.say: Expected number = probability × number of trials.

misconceptions.message: Expected number = probability × trials = 0.2 × 50 = 10. Dividing 50 by 0.2 gives 250, far too many.

bronze.hint: Count how many letter A's, then divide by the total letters.
bronze.display: A letter is chosen at random from MATHEMATICS. Find P(choosing A) as a fraction.

guided_steps.say: Spell out MATHEMATICS and count the letters.

silver.hint: Multiply along the branch: P(H) then P(H) again.
silver.display: A coin is flipped twice. Find P(two heads) as a fraction.

guided_steps.say: Two flips: draw two branches each time. P(H) = 1/2 every flip.
Two heads needs H then H, so multiply along that branch.
Multiply the tops.

misconceptions.message: Two heads needs BOTH flips: 1/2 × 1/2 = 1/4. 1/2 is the chance of just one head.

silver.hint: With replacement the second pick is identical, so multiply the two equal fractions.
silver.display: A bag has 6 red and 4 blue. Two are picked with replacement. Find P(both blue) as a fraction.

guided_steps.say: With replacement the bag is the same each time. P(blue) = 4/10 both picks.
Multiply bottoms, then simplify 16/100 by dividing by 4.

misconceptions.message: The ball is replaced, so the second pick is still 4/10: 4/10 × 4/10 = 4/25. Dropping the total gives 2/15, the without-replacement answer.

silver.hint: Independent AND means multiply the two probabilities.

guided_steps.say: Independent AND means multiply the probabilities.
Now 0.15 = 15/100. Simplify by dividing by 5.

silver.hint: OR with separate colours means add the two probabilities.
silver.display: A bag has 4 red, 3 blue, 3 green. One is picked. Find P(red or green) as a fraction.

guided_steps.say: One pick, two acceptable colours: this is OR, so add the probabilities.
So P(red or green) = 7 over the total.

misconceptions.message: Separate colours on one pick is OR, so add: 4/10 + 3/10 = 7/10. Multiplying gives 12/100 = 3/25.

silver.hint: P(lose) is 3/4 each spin; three losses means cubing it.
silver.display: A spinner has P(win) = ¼. It is spun 3 times. Find P(no wins) as a fraction.

guided_steps.say: No wins in three spins means losing every spin. P(lose) = 1 − 1/4.
Three losses in a row: cube the fraction.
Cube the top.

misconceptions.message: Three spins means cubing: (3/4)³ = 27/64. 3/4 is only one spin.

problem_bank.gold_description: Multi-stage and conditional probability: combine several paths, handle picks without replacement, and use the total-probability rule.
problem_bank.bronze_description: Single-event probability: count the favourable outcomes over the total, then write it as a fraction in its simplest form.
problem_bank.silver_description: Two-stage probability: multiply along the branches of a tree for AND, add branches for OR, and adjust the second fraction when there is no replacement.
